name: Distal Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type 3

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for Distal SMA Type 3

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Electromyographic evidence of chronic denervation and reinnervation consistent with motor neuron disease
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with distal SMA (e.g., DYNC1H1, GARS)
Exclusion of other neuromuscular disorders by clinical, laboratory, and imaging studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal muscle weakness with supportive EMG findings and pathogenic genetic variant identification
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, electrophysiological, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness predominantly in lower limbs
searchTerms: weak muscles at lower limb ends

pathognomonic.symptomName: Muscle atrophy localized to distal extremities
searchTerms: muscle wasting in hands or feet
loss of muscle bulk in extremities

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes in affected limbs

common.symptomName: Foot drop due to distal lower limb weakness
searchTerms: foot drop from weak lower leg muscles
difficulty lifting foot due to weakness
slight sensory changes in hands or feet
muscle cramps in hands and feet

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to distal weakness
searchTerms: difficulty walking due to weak legs
mild muscle weakness near body center
muscle twitching in hands or feet

occasional.symptomName: Joint contractures secondary to muscle wasting
searchTerms: contracted joints due to muscle wasting
limited joint movement from muscle atrophy
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness
swallowing problems due to bulbar weakness

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic and inflammatory causes
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective distal muscle atrophy and fatty replacement
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as DYNC1H1, GARS, or other distal SMA-associated genes
other: Electromyography demonstrating chronic denervation and reinnervation
Nerve conduction studies typically normal or mildly reduced motor amplitudes

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations in PMP22, MPZ, or other CMT genes
Widespread muscle involvement including bulbar muscles

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks to months
Presence of upper motor neuron signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia)
Bulbar symptoms such as severe dysphagia or dysarthria
references: Orphanet: Distal Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type 3 - ORPHA:139547
